chapter_title: Evidence, Motivation, and the Stakeholders of Schooling
learning_objective: The learner will attribute a student's failure on a target concept to its root gap by examining a prerequisite map and a set of pass/fail results, correctly identifying the root gap in at least four of five cases.
specification:
Type: graph-model **sim-id:** prerequisite-chain-diagnosis
**Library:** vis-network
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** attribute
**Learning Objective:** The learner will attribute a student's failure on a target concept to its root gap by examining a prerequisite map and a set of pass/fail results, correctly identifying the root gap in at least four of five cases. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/automating-instructional-design/tree/main/docs/sims/learning-dependency-network
**Prerequisites:** prior knowledge, prerequisite concept, root gap, the meaning of a dependency arrow (all defined in the section "Prior Knowledge and Prerequisite Concepts" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 5 cases, the learner selects exactly one node as the root gap and submits it. A selection is correct when it matches the "Root gap" column in Content. Mastery is 4 of 5 correct. Selecting nodes to read their descriptions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The target concept the student failed is always the place to reteach. (2) Every failed concept needs reteaching. (3) A concept that failed must have a failed prerequisite. **Instructional Rationale:** Attributing a failure to a cause requires reading structure, which here is the prerequisite map. Cases include a root gap at the target itself and cases with several dependent failures, so the learner cannot use a single shortcut. **Content:** Eight nodes, each with its name shown on the node and a one-sentence description shown when it is selected: | # | Node | Description shown | |---|---|---| | 1 | Whole-number multiplication and division | Multiplying and dividing whole numbers fluently. | | 2 | Fractions as parts of a whole | Understanding a fraction as equal parts of one whole. | | 3 | Equivalent fractions | Recognizing that different fractions can name the same amount, such as 1/2 and 2/4. | | 4 | Adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators | Combining fractions after rewriting them with a common denominator. | | 5 | Multiplying and dividing fractions | Multiplying and dividing fractions, including by whole numbers. | | 6 | Ratios | Comparing two quantities, such as 3 apples for every 2 oranges. | | 7 | Unit rates | Finding the amount per one unit, such as price per ounce. | | 8 | Proportional equations | Writing and solving equations that relate two proportional quantities. | Nine arrows, each pointing from a concept to a prerequisite it depends on: | From (depends) | To (prerequisite) | |---|---| | 3 | 1 | | 3 | 2 | | 4 | 3 | | 5 | 1 | | 5 | 2 | | 6 | 3 | | 7 | 5 | | 7 | 6 | | 8 | 7 | Five cases. Each shows a student's pass (P) or fail (F) result on every node, and the target concept the student failed in class: | Case | Target | N1 | N2 | N3 | N4 | N5 | N6 | N7 | N8 | Root gap | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 7 | P | P | P | P | F | P | F | F | 5 | Node 5 failed while both its prerequisites (1 and 2) passed; nodes 7 and 8 fail because they sit above node 5. | | 2 | 8 | P | P | F | F | P | F | F | F | 3 | Node 3 failed while its prerequisites (1 and 2) passed; nodes 4, 6, 7 and 8 fail because they depend on 3, directly or through 6. | | 3 | 4 | P | P | P | F | P | P | P | P | 4 | Node 4 failed while its only prerequisite (3) passed, so the gap is at the target itself. | | 4 | 8 | P | P | P | P | P | P | F | F | 7 | Node 7 failed while both its prerequisites (5 and 6) passed; node 8 fails because it depends on 7. | | 5 | 6 | P | F | F | F | F | F | F | F | 2 | Node 2 has no prerequisites and failed; every other failure lies above it. | **Provenance:** The map is the simplified fractions-to-proportions chain written for this chapter. The pass and fail results are illustrative, and the sim must label them "Illustrative student results." **Rules:** The root gap in a case is the failed node whose direct prerequisites all passed (or that has none). Each case has exactly one root gap. The learner selects one node per case. Nodes with no prerequisites (1 and 2) are visually marked as having none. Zoom and reset are available by buttons; mouse-wheel zoom is disabled. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner explores the map, selecting nodes to read their descriptions. 2. The learner starts the cases. For case 1, the map shows pass/fail marks on every node and highlights the target. 3. The learner selects the node they judge to be the root gap and submits. 4. The sim marks the answer, and highlights the correct node and the failed nodes above it. 5. The learner continues through case 5, then sees the score. 6. The learner should notice that the target concept is the root gap in only one of the five cases. **Feedback:** 5 cases, fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct. [Why text]." Incorrect, selected a failed node whose prerequisite also failed: "That node failed because something below it failed. Look for a failed node whose prerequisites all passed." Incorrect, selected a passed node: "That node passed, so it is not a gap." After the second wrong attempt, the root gap is highlighted with the Why text. Score "n of 5" is shown at the end. **Starting State:** The full map of 8 nodes and 9 arrows is shown with no node selected, and the prompt reads "A student failed one concept. Where should we reteach?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table lists the same eight concepts and the same dependencies. The chapter defines the root gap as a failed concept all of whose prerequisites passed. The mastery bar is 4 of 5.
